mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 5% over two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods when FEDFUNDS > 5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a rise in unemployment (UNRATE > 4%) predicts a negative S&P 500 return over the next 60 trading days due to deteriorating economic fundamentals.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both GDPC1 YoY < -2% and UNRATE > 4%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase of at least 0.3 percentage points in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) for three consecutive months signals weakening labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises by >0.3pp for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods of three consecutive months with UNRATE rising >0.3pp.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% over two consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing output, which is associated with lower corporate earnings and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < previous month -1% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when INDPRO declines by more than 1% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly increase in both personal savings (RSAFS) and the housing starts index (HOUST) by more than 2% signals a shift from consumption to savings and investment, which historically precedes a mild economic expansion and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > previous month +2% AND HOUST > previous month +2%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when both RSAFS and HOUST rise by more than 2% in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp one-month increase in the federal funds rate of more than 0.75 percentage points, in the absence of a concurrent rise in unemployment, signals aggressive tightening that initially shocks equity valuations but ultimately supports returns if inflation expectations fall.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive after a >0.75pp FEDFUNDS rise with flat/unrising UNRATE.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly payroll employment increase (PAYEMS) of more than 1% signals robust labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and corporate profits, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when PAYEMS increases by more than 1% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 4% combined with a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 0.5% in the same month signals stagflation, which historically precedes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL YoY > 4% AND INDPRO < previous month -0.5%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when CPIAUCSL YoY > 4% and INDPRO falls by more than 0.5% in the same month.
